[1] By way of this petition, the petitioners are seeking quashment of award dated 16.11.2015 passed in case No.18/A-82/2014-15 and dated 31.07.2014 passed in case No.01/A-82/2013-14 further Kailash Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114736963/
2 seeking direction to the respondent to return the un-utilized land bearing Survey No.250/1/2.
opennyai_summary.17_January_2023__facts:
[4] According to the petitioner, Late Jamnalal purchased the land from illiterate farmers without complying the provisions of Section 165(6), 165(7-b) of Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959 hence, such sale-deeds are void.
The father of the petitioner Motilal and other land owner filed an appeal before the SDM Rajgarh on the ground that they are illiterate person and they took loan from Jamnalal in the year 2010 and signed the mortgaged documents in order to secure the loan but he got registered a sale-deed in his name.
The compensation was disbursed to the land owners after verification of the revenue records.
After the death of Motilal, name of his son Mahesh was mutated in the revenue record on 16.10.2010, against which the Late Motilal preferred an appeal before the SDO which was dismissed on the ground of delay.
In the appeal, the case of Late Motilal was that the Jamnalal got executed the sale-deed by way of forgery, therefore, he continues to be the owner of the land and without his knowledge the name of Jamnalal has wrongly been mutated hence, it is the case of the petitioners that Jamnalal became the owner by way of registered sale-deeds.
, Late Motilal was only challenging the mutation in the name of Mahesh Prasad or Jamnalal without challenging the sale-deeds.
After dismissal of the appeal by the SDO, an appeal was preferred before the Commissioner by Motilal.
These petitioners have started making complaint in the C.M. Helpline which is not a statutory authority.
[8] If the petitioners are claiming themselves to be legal heir then they should have availed the remedy to challenge the sale-deeds or apply for restoration of the appeal filed by Late Motilal before the Commissioner which was dismissed on 15.11.2017.
There are disputed question of facts involved, therefore, writ petition is not maintainable for want of alternate remedies.
opennyai_summary.17_January_2023__ANALYSIS: [6] So far as challenging the validity of the award passed in the year 2014-15 is concerned, this petition is hopelessly time barred.
opennyai_summary.17_January_2023__decision: In view of the above, Writ Petition is dismissed as not maintainable.

Author: Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari

1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI  &
 HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE DUPPALA VENKATA RAMANA  ON THE 7 th OF AUGUST, 2024  WRIT APPEAL No. 1648 of 2024  KAILASH DANGI AND OTHERS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sameer Saxena, learned counsel for the Petitione  Shri Sudeep Bhargav, Dy. Advocate General for the res  ORDER Per: Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari Heard finally with the consent of parties.
This appeal u/S 2(1) of Madhya Pradesh Uchha Nyayalay (Khand Nyaypith Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam,
2005 has been filed against the order dated 17.01.2023 and 21.03.2024 passed in W.P. No.
24312/2022 and R.P. No. 199/2023.
2.
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
Despite passage of 5 years of acquisition, the land remained unutilized for the purpose for which it was acquired .
Although, as per Section 101 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
return of land can be initiated only after completion of 5 years and, therefore, the cause of action for return of land commences on 17.11.2020.
Writ petition was filed on 27.10.2022 after obtaining certified copies of the awards and revenue records.
Appellants filed complaint before the Chief Minister through CM Helpline, but did not get any relief.
The Sub Divisional Officer was the Land Acquisition Officer dealing with the entire matter of appeal against mutation and objection/representations filed by the aggrieved parties in land acquisition proceedings.
He was well aware of all the facts.
Despite that, compensation was paid.
Learned Single Judge dismissed the petition by holding that the appellants are having remedy to challenge the sale deeds.
Late Motilal on 'patta' and sale deed dated 08.06.2010 was executed without taking permission from the Collector in utter violation of Section 165(6), 165(7-b) of MPLRC and therefore, the same is illegal and void-ab-initio.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that learned Single Judge erred in dismissing the writ petition only on the ground of limitation.
Despite availability of alternative remedy, appellants have approached this Court and therefore, petition was dismissed as not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
Under such circumstances, no interference is warranted in the order passed by learned Single Judge.
The reasons assigned for delay in filing the petition cannot be accepted as no cause of action arises for consideration in the year 2022 for the award passed in the year 2014-15 wherein compensation had also been disbursed.
8. Learned Single Judge has rightly held that when Jamnalal alias Jamnaprasad purchased the land which originally belongs to government and was given on 'patta' to Late Motilal in the year 1984 by registered sale deeds and after the death of Jamnalal, when it got mutated in the name of his son Mahesh in the year 2010, Motilal has challenged the mutation proceedings before the SDO, but the same were dismissed having been filed belatedly.
It has further been held that revenue authorities are not competent to go into veracity of sale deed or to declare the same as null and void and that Motilal should have challenged the sale deeds and not the mutation proceedings.
Even after his death, his legal heirs i.e. the appellants herein should have challenged the sale deeds which has not been done.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Consequently, appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
However, liberty is granted to the appellants to avail appropriate remedy available under the law.
